question: Consider a real valued continuous function \(f\) satisfying \(f(x+1)=f(x)\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R\). Let \(g(t)=\displaystyle\int_0^t f(x)\,dx,\ t\in\mathbb R.\) Define \(h(t)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{g(t+n)}n\), provided the limit exists. Then

options.B: \(h(t)\) is defined only when \(t\) is an integer
options.C: \(h(t)\) is defined for all \(t\in\mathbb R\) and is independent of \(t\)
options.D: none of the above is true.
